subject.title: [Feature]: Expose an inbound non-message event hook to external channel plugins (e.g. reactions)

question: Should external channel plugins surface reactions, edits, receipts, and presence through the existing system-event/inbound-runner APIs, or should OpenClaw add a new public channel event hook or adapter contract?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current public surface is incomplete or under-documented, but choosing between documentation, a `runEvent` dispatch entry, and a new hook/adapter defines long-lived Plugin SDK compatibility semantics.

options.title: Document Existing System Events First
options.body: Treat reactions and similar notifications as routed system events, document the exact external-channel recipe, and only add code if a real plugin sketch proves the recipe insufficient.

options.title: Sponsor A Narrow Event Contract
options.body: Define a typed public event hook or adapter slot for non-message channel activity and require docs, API-baseline, and cross-channel payload tests before implementation lands.

options.title: Align With inbound_activity PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79855 as the starting point, but broaden or narrow it deliberately so debounce activity and agent-visible reaction semantics do not become competing contracts.

recommendation.title: Document Existing System Events First
recommendation.body: Treat reactions and similar notifications as routed system events, document the exact external-channel recipe, and only add code if a real plugin sketch proves the recipe insufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the latest central SDK/channel-runtime commit metadata and prior system-event/channel boundary work, making him the best available routing owner for the SDK direction decision.
